subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Caesarean Indications, Lower Segment, Classical and VBAC

steps.tx: Delivery of the baby through abdominal and uterine incisions is **caesarean section**, indicated when vaginal birth endangers mother or baby. Fetal distress, placenta praevia, transverse lie and failed progress head modern indication lists. Rates above need without benefit harm future pregnancies. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Caesarean section delivers through abdominal incisions when vaginal birth endangers either patient.

steps.tx: The transverse incision in the thin lower uterine segment is the **lower segment caesarean**. It heals strongly, bleeds less and ruptures rarely in future labour. It is the default operation in obstetric practice worldwide. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Lower segment caesarean heals strongly and ruptures rarely in future labour.

steps.tx: The vertical upper segment incision reserved for extreme prematurity, dense adhesions or transverse lie with poor lower segment is the **classical caesarean**. Its scar ruptures in four to nine percent of future pregnancies, so elective repeat delivery precedes labour. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Classical caesarean scars rupture often, so future births are elective repeats.

steps.tx: Vaginal birth after one previous lower segment caesarean is **VBAC**. Planned VBAC succeeds in about three quarters of women, more after any previous vaginal birth. Continuous monitoring and immediate theatre access are conditions of the attempt. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: VBAC succeeds in three quarters with monitoring and immediate theatre access.

steps.tx: The planned labour attempt after caesarean, successful or not, is **TOLAC**. Trial of labour after caesarean distinguishes the attempt from its outcome. Induction and augmentation raise rupture risk and need senior sanction before use. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: TOLAC names the attempt, with induction raising rupture risk needing senior sanction.

steps.tx: Tearing of the caesarean scar in labour, often heralded by fetal bradycardia, is **scar rupture**. Pain, bleeding and recession of the presenting part follow quickly. Category one caesarean and repair, or hysterectomy, resolve the emergency. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Scar rupture heralds with fetal bradycardia and needs category one caesarean.

steps.tx: Silent separation of scar without symptoms found incidentally at surgery is **scar dehiscence**. A window of peritoneum alone covers the fetus. Unlike rupture it needs no emergency action when found at elective surgery. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Scar dehiscence silently separates without symptoms, unlike rupture.

steps.tx: Forceps applied only when the head is on the perineum are **outlet forceps**. Wrigley forceps serve here and for the aftercoming head and caesarean extraction. Their narrow role keeps them the commonest forceps still in use. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Outlet forceps apply only with the head on the perineum.

steps.tx: Urgency categories one to four standardise caesarean communication as **category classification**. Category one means immediate threat to life with a thirty minute decision to delivery ambition. Every unit audits performance against these shared targets. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Category classification standardises caesarean urgency from immediate to elective.
